mappings.note: Names the six Indian soil types by parent rock/deposit (alluvial silt, black volcanic, red iron) and then asks which agroclimatic zone a state falls in. Soil-from-rock is LO-1's rock-types strand, not LO-2 landform formation; the zone-to-state part is locating climatic regions (C-SST1.2-LO-1), not interpreting how climate shapes life.

Sorts vegetables, fruits and trees by the soil type they grow in, so the discriminating knowledge is soil/rock-type identification. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2: the variable held up is soil, not climatic region.

Traces family dishes back through crops to soil types: soil identification (LO-1) plus the crop-to-diet link that is the interrelationship between region and the life of people (C-SST1.2-LO-2). Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, which is map location only.

Asks for modern solutions inspired by traditional practice such as neem-based inputs, i.e. eco-friendly substitution for chemicals. C-SST1.3-LO-3 (sensitivity to conservation) rather than LO-2, because nothing here analyses a pollution source.

Two consecutive deficient monsoons and what disappears from meals is drought consequence, which LO-1 names explicitly among earthquake/flood/drought. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2: the question turns on a hazard event, not on the normal climate of a region.

Classifying one's own state's crops into kharif/rabi/zaid is exactly the climate-to-livelihood interrelationship in India. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, which would require locating the zones on a map rather than reasoning from the season.

The task is to audit what radio and television farm programmes actually convey and categorise it, which is examining the role of media (C-SST4.1-LO-2). Nothing about farming technique is being tested.

Reads an Arthashastra passage on rainfall distribution and asks why the crop cycle needs rain in that pattern: the answer is the climate-crop interrelationship (C-SST1.2-LO-2). CG-SST2 cited at goal level because using an ancient text as a source has no LO in this frame - the CG-SST2 competencies are all kingdoms, monuments and bhakti/sufi.

Kerala rice against Punjab wheat, and what a swap would do, is the textbook form of drawing the interrelationship between climatic region and the life of the people there. Not C-SST1.1-LO-1: soil is one input among climate and rainfall, not the point.

The match-list pairs three cropping seasons (climate-to-crop, C-SST1.2-LO-2) with alluvial and alpine soil and terrace farming (soil/terrain identification, C-SST1.1-LO-1). Both strands are needed to score it.

The taught point is that over 75 percent of rural agricultural workers are women and this is contrary to how farming is pictured - the invisibility of women's labour, which is a consequence of disadvantage (C-SST4.1-LO-1). Not CG-SST4 at goal level, because the LO does reach it.

Correct option is 'regional variations in soil types, climatic zones, terrain and water access', i.e. why agriculture differs region to region. C-SST1.2-LO-2 over LO-1 because no map location is required.

Dating rice cultivation in the Ganga Plain to the 7th-8th millennium BCE from archaeological investigation is pure source-based chronology. Cited at goal level: CG-SST2 covers how historians study the past using different types of sources, but none of its three competencies (administration, monuments, religious movements) reaches prehistoric agriculture.

Tests what Mehrgarh and Harappan evidence does and does not show about barley, millets and vegetables. Goal-level CG-SST2 for the same reason: this frame has no LO for archaeological evidence of early agriculture.
Defines intercropping, a land-and-soil husbandry practice that keeps a field productive. C-SST1.3-LO-3 (conservation sensibility) rather than LO-2, as no pollutant is involved.

Identifies Surapala's Vrikshayurveda as the text prescribing seed treatment, discriminating it from Arthashastra, Amarakosha and Sangam literature - a question about historical texts as sources. Goal-level CG-SST2; no LO covers scientific literature of the past.

Ganga basin issues and proposed remedies - drip irrigation, drought-resistant crops, curbing groundwater pumping - are water-conservation measures. Not LO-2: the answer key argues over-abstraction and dams, not contamination.
Compares the crop list in 'Echoes from the Past' with what is eaten at home to infer continuity of diet over millennia - an inference from historical evidence. Goal-level CG-SST2, as above.

The 46 percent of the working population dependent on agriculture is a livelihood statistic about a section of society. Cited at goal level: CG-SST4 covers the socio-economic role of institutions and the contributions of different sections, but its two competencies are women/media and local markets, neither of which reaches agricultural employment.

Etymology of 'agriculture' from Latin agri and cultura. No LO in this frame addresses the vocabulary or nature of the discipline; CG-SST4 is the nearest goal, agriculture being the economic activity it frames. Flagged as a genuine frame gap rather than a fit.

Distinguishes allied activities (animal husbandry, sericulture, apiculture) from industrial fertiliser manufacture - a classification of economic activity. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers sectors of the economy.

'Why do certain crops thrive in specific regions' is the interrelationship LO almost verbatim. Not C-SST1.1-LO-1, although soil appears in the answer, because temperature and rainfall carry the explanation.

Modern technology's help to farmers spans HYV seeds, machinery, and digital access to weather, market prices and government support - the support-institution side of farming. Goal-level CG-SST4; C-SST4.2-LO-1 is rejected because no local market is being observed.

Why sustainable agriculture matters: soil degradation, groundwater depletion, long-term food security. Squarely LO-3 conservation; LO-2 would need the pollution analysis to be the answer rather than one clause of it.

Farmers' challenges - small holdings, debt, pest attack - and their consequences for food prices and rural livelihoods. Goal-level CG-SST4 for the socio-economic condition of a section of society; no LO covers agrarian distress.
Debate on traditional versus modern irrigation turns on water use, cost and local resources - conservation of water and energy. Not LO-1, as no disaster is in play.

The envisioned future farm is defined by smart irrigation giving water only when needed and reduced weather dependence, i.e. resource efficiency. Conservation LO-3 rather than CG-SST4, because the model answer argues from water and inputs, not from markets or institutions.
The count of India's 15 agroclimatic zones is knowledge of the distribution and extent of climatic regions (C-SST1.2-LO-1). LO-2 is rejected: nothing is inferred about the life of the people.
Contrasts which regions and which crops each monsoon serves - climatic region to cropping life. Not LO-1: the discrimination is by crop and season, not by locating anything.
Names the three cropping seasons, the frame's core climate-to-agriculture content. LO-2 rather than LO-1 for the same reason.
Tamil Nadu and West Bengal grow rice year round because both monsoons reach them - a regional climate explaining a regional cropping pattern. Not LO-1, which would stop at locating those states.
Infers the rabi season from a crop's temperature and water needs. Reasoning from climate to farming practice, so LO-2.
Defines zaid as the short summer season between rabi and kharif, with its characteristic crops - seasonal climate to crop choice. LO-2.

Sikkim as the first fully organic state rests on banning chemical fertilisers and pesticides: a listed measure against chemical contamination (LO-2) taken as a conservation commitment (LO-3). Both cited because the fact is the ban and the point is the conservation stance.
Assertion-reason on kharif vulnerability to monsoon timing and volume. LO-2 rather than LO-1 because the reasoning is about normal seasonal dependence, not about a drought event.
Recovers the pre-Arabic Sanskrit season names haimana, kedara and graishmika from older texts. Historical terminology from sources; goal-level CG-SST2, as no LO reaches it.
Correct option identifies soil as the upper crust layer supplying nutrients, water and support - soil as a material of the earth's surface. C-SST1.1-LO-1; LO-2 would require a landform to be forming.
Counts India's six major soil types. Identification of soil/rock types, LO-1.
Matches each soil to its parent material and fertility (alluvial = river silt, black = volcanic, red = iron-bearing). Rock-and-soil-type identification, LO-1.
Red soil's colour traced to iron reacting with air and water - composition of a soil type, LO-1 not LO-2.

Defines weathering as the process breaking rock down into particles. Cited to LO-2 (formation due to various factors) rather than LO-1, because the question tests the process, not the identity of a rock or soil.
Crop rotation prevents exhaustion of specific soil nutrients - a soil conservation rationale. LO-3; LO-2 is rejected as nothing is polluted.
Contour ploughing along hill curves to stop rainwater carrying soil away is erosion control. LO-3 conservation, not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the question asks for the remedy, not how the slope formed.

Panchagavya's five ingredients - a traditional biofertiliser replacing chemical input. LO-3 conservation of soil and its organisms. (Answer key on this row belongs to a different question; see report.)

Stem survives only as a fragment, but options and key show a match-list of crop rotation, multiple cropping, contour ploughing and organic fertilisers against their soil benefits - all soil conservation, LO-3.
Fragmentary stem; the key resolves it to Green Revolution / HYV seeds / organic farming / Sikkim. Cited to LO-3 because the pairing's through-line is the shift from chemical to natural methods.

Matches apiculture, pisciculture, sericulture and horticulture to their meanings - allied livelihoods that support farming families. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO in this frame covers sectors of rural economic activity.
Matches kharif, rabi and zaid to monsoon, winter and summer. Pure climate-to-cropping, LO-2.
Drip irrigation delivering water to the roots to maximise efficiency is water conservation. LO-3, distinguished from the traditional-versus-modern debate item only by depth, not by outcome.
Beejamrit as an organic cow-dung seed coating, an input that substitutes for chemical seed treatment. LO-3; LO-2 rejected as no contamination is analysed.

The criticism is that non-viable hybrid seed forces annual repurchase and financial dependence on seed corporations - a market-power argument. Goal-level CG-SST4 (socio-economic role of market institutions); C-SST4.2-LO-1 is rejected because it is a field visit to a local market, not the seed trade.

The ancient Indian seed drill combining tillage, sowing and furrow closing - technology recovered from the historical record. Goal-level CG-SST2; C-SST2.2-LO-1 is temples, tombs and mosques only, so it cannot take agricultural technology.
Gokrishi integrates cattle for manure and draught, closing the nutrient loop without external input. LO-3 conservation.

Assertion-reason on the Green Revolution delivering food self-sufficiency through HYV seeds, chemicals and machinery - a state-led programme's socio-economic outcome. Goal-level CG-SST4 rather than CG-SST2, since the question asks what the programme achieved, not how the past is known.

Identifies M.S. Swaminathan as architect of the Green Revolution. Goal-level CG-SST4 for its 'recognises the contributions of different sections of society' clause; no LO covers individual contributors.

Sorts real long-term harms of the Green Revolution - soil impoverishment, pesticide contamination of water, groundwater depletion - from a distractor. Pesticide contamination is LO-2; soil and groundwater depletion is LO-3; both are needed to eliminate the options.

Hydroponics as soil-free growing in nutrient solution. No LO covers agricultural technology, so cited to LO-3 as a land-and-water-efficient method; C-SST1.1-LO-1 is rejected because the question defines the method, not a soil.

FAO heritage systems - Kashmir saffron, Odisha forest-integrated farming, Kerala below-sea-level farming - each a region's climate and terrain producing a distinctive farming life. LO-2 rather than LO-1, which would stop at locating them.
Bananas on paddy bunds act as windbreaks and stabilise bund soil against erosion, with income as a bonus. Soil conservation, LO-3; the income clause is secondary and does not carry CG-SST4.
Average holding down to about three-quarters of a hectare through generational division - the economic condition of farming households. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers landholding.
